author: reek
body: The grammar is record = field *(COMMA field). A separator is always followed by a field and that field may be empty, so a record ending in a comma has an empty last field and a record that is one comma has two of them. Those two were the defect: the row loop ended at the input without recording that it had just stepped over a separator, so the final empty field was never pushed.

author: reek
body: The other five parse lines are the control. They were correct before the fix and must stay correct, which is what separates a repair from a rewrite that moves everything.

author: reek
body: The emit lines are checked the other way round. Each was fed to an independent CSV parser on the host, which must recover exactly the fields that went in; quoting only when required, and doubling an embedded quote, are what that parser is being asked to confirm. A round trip through this chapter's own two halves would prove neither, because both halves can share an assumption and agree forever.
